title: Dengue Fever: Assessment, Warning Signs and Admission Criteria

evidenceAudit.scope: Adults and children with suspected dengue in Saudi Arabia in primary care, the emergency department (ED) or hospital: case definition, clinical phases, warning signs, severity grouping (A, B, C), laboratory confirmation, fluid management, discharge criteria and public health notification. Uses the Saudi Public Health Authority (PHA) and Ministry of Health (MOH) dengue guidance version 1.3 (2023) and the paracetamol product information. Paediatric fluid rates follow the same per-kilogram schedule given by PHA; paediatric paracetamol dosing is not listed.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-21.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: PHA 2023 lists 0.9% saline and Ringer's lactate as isotonic choices without ranking them; 0.9% saline, the first listed, is marked preferred.
PHA 2023 gives paracetamol maximum 4 g per day for adults and says children are dosed accordingly; paediatric paracetamol doses are not listed here.
Advice to avoid non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs and intramuscular injections in dengue was not found in the opened PHA guidance and is not included.
Colloid choice and blood product thresholds beyond those in PHA 2023 page 27 are not given.
Typical normal ranges for white cells, platelets, haematocrit and transaminases are not from PHA; local laboratory ranges apply.

pathophysiology.summary: Dengue is caused by four serotypes (DENV 1 to 4) of a flavivirus spread by female Aedes aegypti mosquitoes; one person can be infected more than once (PHA dengue guidance 2023, Section Introduction and Section Mode of Transmission). After 5 to 7 days (range 3 to 14) incubation, a febrile phase of 2 to 7 days may include petechiae and mucosal bleeding (PHA dengue guidance 2023, Section Clinical Phases). The critical phase comes at defervescence on days 3 to 7, when temperature falls to 37.5 to 38 °C; plasma leakage can then cause shock within 24 to 48 hours of warning signs (PHA dengue guidance 2023, Section Clinical Phases). In recovery over the next 48 to 72 hours, fluid returns to the circulation; white cells recover before platelets (PHA dengue guidance 2023, Section Clinical Phases). Rising haematocrit with a fast fall in platelets reflects plasma leakage (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 11).

symptoms: Fever above 38.5 °C with headache, retro-orbital pain, joint and muscle pain, nausea, vomiting, swollen glands or rash (PHA dengue guidance 2023, Section Case Definition).
Persistent vomiting and severe abdominal pain are warning signs (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 24).
Lethargy or restlessness is a warning sign (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 24).
physicalSigns: Rash; in recovery, a rash of isles of white in a sea of red (PHA dengue guidance 2023, Section Clinical Phases).
Positive tourniquet test (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 11).
Mucosal bleeding, petechiae, bruising (PHA dengue guidance 2023, Section Clinical Phases and p. 9).
Liver enlargement more than 2 cm and clinical fluid accumulation are warning signs (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 24).
Shock and falling blood pressure in severe dengue (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 9).
redFlags: Any warning sign: persistent vomiting, severe abdominal pain or tenderness, mucosal bleed, lethargy or restlessness, fluid accumulation, liver above 2 cm, rising haematocrit with rapid platelet fall (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 24).
Severe plasma leakage with shock or fluid accumulation with respiratory distress (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 11).
Severe organ involvement: aspartate aminotransferase (AST) or alanine aminotransferase (ALT) 1000 or more, impaired consciousness, heart involvement (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 11).
precipitants: Living in or travelling within 15 days to an endemic area (PHA dengue guidance 2023, Section Case Definition).
Mosquito breeding near home or work (PHA dengue guidance 2023, Section Case Definition).
Pregnancy, infancy, old age, diabetes mellitus and renal failure raise risk and move the patient to hospital care (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 26).
Living alone or far from hospital (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 26).

differentials.condition: Other viral haemorrhagic fevers (chikungunya, yellow fever, West Nile, Zika, Alkhurma, Rift Valley, Crimean-Congo)
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Negative dengue reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR), non-structural protein 1 (NS1) antigen and immunoglobulin M (IgM); PHA screens a share of negative cases for these (PHA dengue guidance 2023, Section Criteria for Screening Other Viral Hemorrhagic Fever).

differentials.condition: Other flavivirus infection with cross-reacting IgM
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: IgM cross-reacts with Zika, West Nile, yellow fever and Alkhurma; send confirmed specimens to the public health laboratory (PHA dengue guidance 2023, Section Case Definition footnote).
Fever with 2 of aches, rash, nausea or vomiting, positive tourniquet test, leucopenia, and no warning sign (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 11).

ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Request on days 1 to 5; stays positive up to day 12 (PHA dengue guidance 2023, Section Laboratory Tests, p. 12).

ruleIn.testName: Full blood count: white cells and platelets
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Leucopenia supports diagnosis; rapid platelet fall with rising haematocrit is a warning sign; daily in Group A (PHA dengue guidance 2023, pp. 11, 24 and 25).
ruleIn.normalValue: White cells 4.0 to 11.0 × 10⁹/L; platelets 150 to 400 × 10⁹/L (typical adult ranges)

clinicalManagement.title: Suspect, test and notify
actions: Apply the case definition and ask about endemic exposure in the last 15 days (PHA dengue guidance 2023, Section Case Definition).
Send two samples for RT-PCR, NS1 and IgM (PHA dengue guidance 2023, Section Reporting).
Notify immediately through HESN Plus using the viral haemorrhagic fever form (PHA dengue guidance 2023, Section Reporting).

clinicalManagement.title: Look for warning signs and assign a group
actions: Check for warning signs and co-existing conditions (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 24).
No warning signs and able to drink and pass urine at least every 6 hours: Group A, home care (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 25).
Warning signs or co-existing conditions: Group B, admit (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 26).
Shock, severe bleeding or organ impairment: Group C, admit (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 27).

clinicalManagement.title: Group A: home care
clinicalManagement.timeframe: Daily review until out of the critical phase
actions: Advise bed rest, enough fluid and paracetamol (see Medicines) (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 25).
Review daily for falling white cells, defervescence and warning signs; give a home care card and advise immediate return if warning signs appear (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 25).
Send home only if haematocrit is stable (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 25).

clinicalManagement.title: Group B: in-hospital fluids
actions: Co-existing conditions without warning signs: encourage oral fluids; if not tolerated, give intravenous 0.9% saline or Ringer's lactate at maintenance rate (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 26).
Warning signs: take a reference haematocrit, then give isotonic crystalloid on the stepped schedule (see Medicines) (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 26).

clinicalManagement.title: Group C: treat shock
actions: Compensated shock: isotonic crystalloid 5 to 10 mL/kg/hour over 1 hour, then step down (see Medicines) (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 27).
Hypotensive shock: crystalloid or colloid 20 mL/kg bolus over 15 minutes (see Medicines) (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 27).
Bleeding: 5 to 10 mL/kg fresh packed red cells or 10 to 20 mL/kg fresh whole blood (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 27).
Haematocrit below 40% in children and adult women or below 45% in adult men during instability suggests bleeding: cross-match and transfuse (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 27).

clinicalManagement.title: Discharge
actions: Discharge when the discharge criteria are met (see Disposition) (PHA dengue guidance 2023, Section Patient Discharge Criteria).

regimens.indication: Fever and pain in dengue without warning signs
regimens.dose: 1 g (two 500 mg tablets) every 4 hours as needed, no more than 4 doses in 24 hours (Paracetamol SmPC, Section 4.2); maximum 4 g per day in adults (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 25).
regimens.duration: While febrile; review if needed for more than 3 days (Paracetamol SmPC, Section 4.2)
adjustments: Care in severe hepatic or renal impairment (Paracetamol SmPC, Section 4.2).
Higher hepatotoxicity risk with regular alcohol excess, enzyme-inducing drugs, malnutrition or low glutathione (Paracetamol SmPC, Sections 4.4 and 4.9).
Children: dose by age and weight per formulary (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 25).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Total daily paracetamol from all products.
Daily dengue review for warning signs (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 25).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to paracetamol or excipients (Paracetamol SmPC, Section 4.3).

regimens.patientGroup: Adults and children with Group B dengue and warning signs
regimens.dose: After a reference haematocrit: 5 to 7 mL/kg/hour for 1 to 2 hours, then 3 to 5 mL/kg/hour for 2 to 4 hours, then 2 to 3 mL/kg/hour or less. If haematocrit is unchanged or rises slightly, continue 2 to 3 mL/kg/hour for 2 to 4 hours; if vital signs worsen and haematocrit rises fast, increase to 5 to 10 mL/kg/hour for 1 to 2 hours (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 26).
regimens.duration: Through the critical phase; reduce gradually as leakage settles (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 26)
adjustments: Reassess clinical state and repeat haematocrit before each change (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 26).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Vital signs and peripheral perfusion every 1 to 4 hours until out of the critical phase (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 26).
Urine output every 4 to 6 hours (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 26).
Haematocrit before and after each fluid step, then every 6 to 12 hours (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 26).
contraindications: Fluid accumulation with respiratory distress signals severe plasma leakage; reduce fluids gradually as leakage falls towards the end of the critical phase (PHA dengue guidance 2023, pp. 26 to 27).
A falling haematocrit with instability suggests bleeding: cross-match and transfuse rather than give more crystalloid (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 27).

regimens.patientGroup: Adults and children with Group C dengue, hypotensive shock
regimens.dose: 20 mL/kg bolus over 15 minutes. If better: 10 mL/kg/hour for 1 hour, then reduce gradually. If still unstable with high haematocrit: colloid 10 to 20 mL/kg over 1 hour as a second bolus, then 7 to 10 mL/kg/hour for 1 to 2 hours (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 27).
adjustments: Review the haematocrit taken before the first bolus to separate leakage from bleeding (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 27).

medicationPlan.note: No antiviral treatment exists; care is supportive (PHA dengue guidance 2023, Section Introduction). Fluid rates are per kilogram and apply to adults and children as written by PHA. diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Fever above 38.5 °C with one or more of headache, joint and muscle pain, retro-orbital pain, nausea, vomiting, swollen glands or rash (PHA dengue guidance 2023, Section Case Definition).
Suspected case with mosquito index at home or work, or travel to an endemic area in the last 15 days (PHA dengue guidance 2023, Section Case Definition).
Suspected case with positive RT-PCR, NS1 antigen or IgM (PHA dengue guidance 2023, Section Case Definition).
No warning signs, drinking enough and passing urine at least every 6 hours (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 25).
Warning signs, or pregnancy, infancy, old age, diabetes, renal failure, or social risk (PHA dengue guidance 2023, pp. 24 and 26).
Severe plasma leakage with shock or respiratory distress, severe bleeding or severe organ impairment (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 27).

teaching.scope: Adults and children with suspected dengue in Saudi Arabia in primary care, the emergency department (ED) or hospital: case definition, clinical phases, warning signs, severity grouping (A, B, C), laboratory confirmation, fluid management, discharge criteria and public health notification. Uses the Saudi Public Health Authority (PHA) and Ministry of Health (MOH) dengue guidance version 1.3 (2023) and the paracetamol product information. Paediatric fluid rates follow the same per-kilogram schedule given by PHA; paediatric paracetamol dosing is not listed.
learningObjectives: Apply the Saudi dengue case definition and confirm with NS1, RT-PCR or IgM.
Know the three phases and when the critical phase starts.
Recognise warning signs and assign Group A, B or C.
Titrate fluids to haematocrit and clinical state.
pitfalls: Sending home a patient with warning signs.
Giving large fluid volumes without haematocrit checks.
Using a single IgG result to diagnose acute dengue.
keyPoints: Danger comes as the fever falls (days 3 to 7).
Rising haematocrit with falling platelets means leakage.
A falling haematocrit in shock suggests bleeding.

patientEducation: Dengue is spread by mosquitoes that bite during the day.
Drink plenty of fluids, rest and take paracetamol only.
Return at once for vomiting, belly pain, bleeding, drowsiness or reduced urine, especially as the fever settles.
Use window screens and repellents; empty and clean water containers weekly (PHA dengue guidance 2023, Section Prevention).
lifestyleAndDiet: Bed rest and enough fluids (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 25).
Avoid traumatic activities for 1 to 2 weeks if platelets are still low at discharge (PHA dengue guidance 2023, Section Patient Discharge Criteria).
mdtReferrals: Primary care or emergency physician; infectious diseases or internal medicine; intensive care for Group C; infection control officer and public health coordinator for notification (PHA dengue guidance 2023, Section Reporting).
dischargeCriteria: No fever for at least 24 hours without antipyretics; appetite back; visible improvement; good urine output; at least 2 to 3 days after recovery from shock; no respiratory distress from effusion and no ascites; platelets above 50,000/mm³ (PHA dengue guidance 2023, Section Patient Discharge Criteria, p. 28).
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Group A: daily review until out of the critical period; all: inform the patient of final laboratory results and give prevention education (PHA dengue guidance 2023, p. 25 and Section Reporting).
